test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Consider a situation where a person is sitting in a car and is driving at a constant velocity in a straight line. If the car turns sharply to the left, the person will be pushed in which of the following directions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a car makes a sharp turn, the passengers inside experience a force due to inertia.
 
• This force is a result of the body's tendency to maintain its state of motion, as per Newton's First Law of Motion.
 
• If the car turns left, inertia causes the person to be pushed towards the right.
 
• This perceived force pushing the person to the right is often referred to as a "centrifugal force" in a non-inertial reference frame.
 
• The actual cause is the car moving left while the person's body tends to continue in a straight line.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion (Law of Inertia)**

 
 
• States that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• This law explains why passengers move in the opposite direction of the turn.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal Force**
 
 
• It is a perceived force that acts outward on a body moving around a center, arising from the body's inertia.
 
• It is not a real force but rather a result of the inertia of the body in a rotating reference frame.
 
 
 
• **Inertial Reference Frame**
 
 
• A frame of reference in which Newton's laws of motion hold true.
 
• In such frames, objects not acted upon by forces move in straight lines at constant speeds.
 
 
 
• **Non-Inertial Reference Frame**
 
 
• A frame of reference that is accelerating or rotating.
 
• In these frames, fictitious forces, such as centrifugal force, are introduced to explain motion.
